parts.title: My home is an island
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I live on a tiny island in the north of Scotland. Only two hundred people live here, and most of us know each other well. Our school has just twelve pupils, and I am in the same class as my little cousin.

The ferry is the most important thing in our lives. It comes three times a week, and it brings food, post and visitors. If the weather is bad, it cannot sail, and then we have to wait. Last winter, there was no ferry for nine days, and the shop ran out of bread!

Some people think that island life must be boring, but I disagree. After school, I go to the beach with my friends to look for crabs and shells. In the evening, we play football on the grass by the church. In summer, the sun does not go down until almost midnight.

Of course, there are some things I miss. There is no cinema, and the nearest big town is three hours away by boat and bus. When I am eighteen, I will probably go to university on the mainland. But I know that I will always come back, because this is my home.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about her school?
options: It has only twelve pupils in total
It is in the same building as the church
It is closed during the winter months
questions.explanation: Our school has just twelve pupils.

questions.prompt: What happened last winter?
options: The ferry could not sail for nine days
The shop was closed for a week
The island lost its power for a day
questions.explanation: There was no ferry for nine days, and the shop ran out of bread.

questions.prompt: What does she do after school?
options: She helps her cousin with homework
She looks for crabs and shells
She works in the island shop
questions.explanation: She goes to the beach with friends to look for crabs and shells.

questions.prompt: What does she miss about the mainland?
questions.explanation: There is no cinema on the island.

questions.prompt: What does the writer think about her future?
options: She will leave and never return
She will start a business on the island
She will return to her home one day
questions.explanation: She says she will always come back, because this is her home.

parts.title: A holiday on a tiny island
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Coral Cay is a tiny island in the Caribbean. It is only two kilometres long, and you can walk all the way round it in about an hour. [1] There are no big hotels, no cars and no traffic lights.

Most visitors arrive on the little boat from the larger island. [2] The journey takes thirty minutes, and passengers often see dolphins on the way.

There are only five places to sleep on the island. [3] Most of them have a view of the sea from every window, and the owners cook breakfast for each guest.

During the day, visitors swim, rest in the shade or take a small boat to a nearby reef. [4] The water is so clear that you can see the fish from the beach.

In the evening, everyone eats together on the sand. [5] Many people say that it is the most relaxing holiday they have ever had.
sentences: This makes it one of the quietest places that you can find.
It leaves every morning at nine and returns at five.
All of them are small family houses near the beach.
There are many shops in the centre of the capital.
Even in the hottest weather, there is a nice cool breeze.
Afterwards, they sit and watch the stars come out.

gaps.explanation: The island is tiny, so it is one of the quietest places, and the next sentence lists what it does not have.
The boat leaving at nine matches "the little boat", and the journey then takes thirty minutes.
The five places to sleep are small family houses, which explains the owners and the sea views.
The breeze after swimming and resting in the shade connects to the clear water in the next sentence.
Watching the stars after eating together leads to the comment on a relaxing holiday.

parts.title: Why people love islands
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Islands have always been popular places for holidays. People like them [1] they are often quiet and beautiful. On a small island, you can leave your bike outside your door, and nobody will take it. Life moves [2] a slower speed, and people have time to talk to each other. [3] you are tired of busy cities, an island holiday can be a perfect rest. However, living on an island is not always easy. Everything has to come [4] boat, so shopping can be expensive. Young people sometimes leave to find work on the mainland, and [5] is a problem for small communities. Even so, those [6] stay usually say that they would not live anywhere else.

gaps.explanation: People like them because they are quiet: reason.
If you are tired of busy cities: condition.
The preposition "by" goes with transport: come by boat.
This is a problem refers back to young people leaving.
Those who stay: relative pronoun for people.

parts.title: A talk about Iceland
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: Good morning, everyone. In today's lesson, I will tell you about Iceland, a large island in the North Atlantic Ocean. About four hundred thousand people live there, and more than half of them live in the capital city, Reykjavik. The island has more than a hundred volcanoes, and some of them are still active. Many people also enjoy bathing in hot pools, which are heated naturally by the ground. In summer, the sun hardly goes down at all, so there are almost twenty-four hours of daylight. In winter, it is the opposite, and the days are very short. The most popular food is fish, and Icelandic people eat it in many different ways. If you visit in winter, you may see the northern lights, which are green and pink lights in the sky. Many tourists say that this is the most beautiful thing they have ever seen.

gaps.explanation: About four hundred thousand people live there.

gaps.prompt: There are more than a hundred ___
gaps.explanation: The island has more than a hundred volcanoes.

gaps.prompt: Hot pools are heated by the ___
gaps.explanation: Hot pools, which are heated naturally by the ground.
The most popular food is fish.

gaps.prompt: In winter, you may see the northern ___
gaps.explanation: You may see the northern lights.

parts.title: An interview with a lighthouse keeper
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Ainsley, you live and work on a very small island. How long have you been here?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: Nineteen years now. I came for one summer as a volunteer, and I never left.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What does your job involve?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: I check the light every evening and clean it every week. The lamp is automatic now, but boats still need someone to look after it, especially in storms.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Is it lonely?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: Sometimes, but there are four other families here, and we eat together every Sunday. I also talk to my daughter on the phone each night.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the best thing about island life?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: The silence. In the city, I could never hear the sea at night. Here, it is the first sound I hear when I wake up.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: And what is the worst thing?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: The wind. In winter, it blows for days and the house shakes. Last year, a window broke and I had to fix it in the dark.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do many tourists visit?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: In summer, about thirty come every week. I show them the top of the lighthouse, and they take photos. It is the only time that I need to wear a clean shirt.
